archetype.name: Play-In Team (whistle-driven)
archetype.definition: A roughly league-average team in the East's crowded middle, a step up from three bottom-finish seasons, whose offense leans on getting to the free-throw line rather than on shooting.

report.headline: Three games in, last year's 17-win team looks like a league-average one.
report.take:
Washington has spent three straight seasons at the very bottom of the site's rankings: 15-67, 18-64 and 17-65, with last year's Def Rank 30 and a DRtg of 122.7. Through three games the profile is unrecognizable. A Net Rtg of 1.9 ranks 13th, the offense (ORtg 112.9, 12th) and defense (DRtg 111, 13th) both sit just on the good side of the league line, and the 2-1 record matches the margin exactly, with W vs Pt Diff at 0. This is not a team winning coin flips. It is a middling team that happens to be playing in a three-way tie atop the Southeast.

The offense has an unmistakable signature: a FT Rate of 40.2, first in the league and well above the league average of 29.9, from a team that sat at 23.5 last season. That free-throw volume is why TS % (58.1, 14th) runs ahead of a below-average eFG % (51.7, 18th). It is papering over awful perimeter shooting. A 3P % of 28.6 ranks 27th, on a low 3PA Rate. The pace is quick at 104.5, and Trae Young's 34 assists say the ball runs through him, while Anthony Davis carries a USG % of 30.6.

The numbers hide two things. First, the three-point lines are noise pulling in opposite directions. The team's own 3P % should climb toward last year's 35.9. The Opp 3P % of 28.8 (4th) should drift back toward last year's 36.8. Most of the improved defense on paper is opponents missing jumpers, so expect those two to roughly cancel. Second, the lineup data is upside down. The heavy-minute starters (Young at -22.7 On-Off, Davis at -21.5, Coulibaly at -20.6) have been outscored, while Justin Champagnie (+43.6, 4th of 73 on the SF tab) and the young guards off the bench have been the best units. Davis's 49.1 TS % and -6.6 BPM won't stay that low if he's healthy, so the starting group should improve, but three games of On-Off is mostly noise.

Where this is heading is somewhere between the 55-win pace the sheet extrapolates and the 17-win past. A C-graded frontcourt, weak offensive rebounding (ORB % 23, 25th) and a defense that forces few turnovers argue against a real contender. A top-tier whistle and a backcourt graded B argue against a return to the bottom. Play-in range is the honest read until the shooting normalizes and the sample grows.

strengths.title: League's best at drawing fouls
strengths.body: A FT Rate of 40.2 leads the league, far above the league average, and it's the reason a below-average eFG % still produces a top-half TS %. It reflects a deliberate attack-the-paint style with high-usage creators. It will likely come down from first in the league over a full season, but it marks a clear break from last season's 23.5, and some of it should stick.

strengths.title: A defense that is finally respectable
strengths.body: A DRtg of 111 ranks 13th after last season's 122.7, the league's worst. The Opp eFG % of 49.8 (8th) looks great, but much of it comes from opponents' 28.8% from three, which is luck as much as scheme. A middle-of-the-pack defense is believable. A top-ten one isn't yet.

strengths.title: Champagnie and the bench units
strengths.body: Justin Champagnie ranks 4th of 73 on the SF tab with 28 rebounds in 69 minutes and a +43.6 On-Off. Bub Carrington, Tre Johnson and Kyshawn George all have positive On-Off marks too. The magnitudes are three-game noise, but the direction says the second unit's energy and rebounding travel.

concerns.title: Broken three-point shooting, low volume
concerns.body: A 3P % of 28.6 ranks 27th, and the 3PA Rate of 37.8 is also below the league. The offense is neither making threes nor taking many. Shooting should recover toward last year's 35.9, but if the free throws dry up there isn't a perimeter game to fall back on.

concerns.title: Starters getting outscored, Davis inefficient
concerns.body: Davis has used possessions at a 30.6 USG % with a 49.1 TS % and -6.6 BPM, and the starters' On-Off marks are deeply negative. Three games is far too few to trust On-Off, and Davis's efficiency should rise. But until the primary scorers produce, the team's net rating depends on bench minutes.

concerns.title: Soft frontcourt and the glass
concerns.body: The frontcourt grades C, the team rebounds only 23% of its own misses (25th), and opponents take a large share of shots at the rim (Opp Rim Rate 33.7, 22nd). Opposing power forwards have scored well above their own averages. This matches a structural thinness up front, and it's the weakness most likely to last.

trend.note: A win, a loss, a win, with a margin that matches the record. There's no streak to speak of, just a team playing like a league-average side after three years at the bottom.

weekAhead.headline: Two shots at overrated Charlotte, one real test in Cleveland
weekAhead.body:
Four games, three on the road, but the opponents are kind. Charlotte, faced twice, is 2-1 on a Net Rtg of -11.7 with the league's best W vs Pt Diff. That record is running well ahead of its play, and its ORtg of 102.3 ranks 29th. Orlando is 1-2 with a 26th-ranked offense. Washington's Net Rtg is better than all three opponents', so a 3-1 week is within reach and anything worse than 2-2 would be a warning sign.

Cleveland is the hinge. The Cavaliers allow the league's lowest Opp Rim FG % (49.3) and have an A- frontcourt, which hits Washington's foul-drawing, paint-attacking offense head on. Orlando also brings an A- frontcourt, so two of the four games test the C-graded group up front.

keyMatchups.title: Charlotte's threes against luck-aided defense
keyMatchups.body: Charlotte takes the league's highest share of its shots from three (3PA Rate 53) but converts poorly and rarely gets to the line. Washington's 28.8% Opp 3P % is the stat most likely to regress, and a volume-shooting opponent is where that could show. Still, Charlotte's offense has been among the league's worst.

keyMatchups.title: Cleveland's rim wall vs the whistle
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland leads the league in Opp Rim FG %, so Davis and the drivers will meet resistance. The opening is on the wing: the Cavaliers have allowed opposing small forwards 41 points a game, the most in the league, and grade D at the position. That suits Coulibaly and Champagnie.

keyMatchups.title: Orlando's guards are exposed
keyMatchups.body: Orlando's backcourt grades D, and its defense has given opposing shooting guards 42.67 points a game, 27th in the league. George and Johnson should find room. The Magic's A- frontcourt is the counterweight on the glass.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the free-throw rate holds up in Cleveland against the league's stingiest rim defense.

restOfSeason.body:
The sheet's 55-win pace is a three-game extrapolation and shouldn't be taken literally. The parts that look real are the style (heavy free-throw volume, a fast pace) and a defense that is no longer a sieve. The parts that will move are the three-point percentages on both ends. Washington's own shooting should rise and opponents' should too, which leaves the net rating roughly where it is, near zero. The frontcourt grade, poor offensive rebounding and low forced-turnover rate cap the ceiling.

Expect something like 31 to 41 wins and a Net Rtg between about -3.5 and +1. That is a huge leap from 17 wins and squarely in play-in territory. Health and Davis's efficiency decide which end of that range it lands on.
swingFactors: Whether the free-throw volume holds over a full season

confidence.note: Three games; On-Off and three-point numbers are mostly noise.
